newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico tells 12 European rights activists to leave.
newsitem.headline: Mexico tells 12 European rights activists to leave.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1997-05-02

text.p: Mexico has ordered 12 Europeans who were working with Indian communities in the troubled southeastern state of Chiapas to leave the country, the Europeans said on Friday.

The 12 -- four Spaniards, three Germans, two Italians, two French and one Dutch person -- said Mexican migration officials told them to leave by midday on Saturday for carrying out "activities unauthorised by the visa used to enter the country."
It was the latest in a series of expulsions of foreign human rights officials in recent weeks in southern Mexico where left-wing rebel groups have sprung up in recent years.

In late April, a member of the U.S.-based Unitarian Universalist Service Committee and two Central American rights workers were given 72 hours to leave the country for using the wrong type of visa while carrying out investigations in the states of Oaxaca and Guerrero. All three left.

Officials of Mexico's National Migration Institute told the Europeans, "It is not an expulsion, it is an invitation to leave the country," one of the Spaniards, who asked not to be identified, told reporters.

He said the 12 were travelling on tourist visas, and that they were interrogated by migration officials after taking part in an anti-government rally organised by supporters of the rebel Zapatista National Liberation Army last week.
The Zapatistas launched an uprising in the mountains of Chiapas state, bordering Guatemala, in January 1994, and are now surrounded by the army, awaiting a renewal of peace talks with the government.
